extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in wartime/current affairs
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item newspaper page of wartime news dispatches and human-interest reports (AP/Associated Press), covering military operations, government policy debates, awards, civil disturbances in POW camps, and local wartime impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Geneva Convention / attack only military objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Our flyers who attacked Tokyo were instructed to attack only military objectives; the Secretary said he was 'very loath to believe that Japan' would violate rules of the Geneva convention governing the conduct of war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/context in article: US officials emphasize adherence to international law as a defense against Japanese radio accusations that airmen committed 'inhuman acts' against civilians; reporters quote Secretary Stimson noting instructions given to aircrews and asserting reports that they struck military targets 'with remarkable accuracy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: War Department policy on wording and release of information
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Department’s policy of wording all information (about operations and personnel) to control what is released to the public and avoid compromising operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: referenced in connection with announcements about airmen and raids; implies a policy to withhold or carefully phrase operational and casualty details to avoid aiding the enemy or causing confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation banning sale of hard liquor at Army camps / proposed prohibition amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sale of hard liquor at Army camps is barred by regulation; Senator Lee offered an amendment to ban sales, gifts or use of all alcoholic drink from Army and Navy reservations and adjacent areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article records the debate over the Lee amendment (which would extend/clarify prohibition near military sites), arguments for military efficiency and health versus concerns about creating a national 'prohibition' precedent, and the Senate's procedural decision to send the amendment to the military committee for hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beverage policy on naval vessels (contrast to Army camp regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The article states that beverages in any form were allowed on naval vessels while sale of hard liquor at Army camps was barred by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as part of reporting on differences in service policies and on criticisms/rumors about 'loafing' in shipyards; used to contextualize debates about morale and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisoner-of-war camp management: shackling, response to resistance, and use of force
rubrics_metrics.description: At Bowmanville (Ont.) POW camp guards ordered shackling of prisoners; prisoners forcibly resisted, barricaded themselves, and guards fired four warning shots (three in the air, one toward the ground) and later reinforced the guard to restore order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government statement noted injuries on both sides, hunger strike by some prisoners, minor wounds from ricochet, property damage, and that normal life resumed after reinforcements; this conveys the procedural standard that shackling may be ordered and warning shots/reinforcements used if prisoners resist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for awarding military decorations (as reported)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards such as Silver Stars and the Distinguished Flying Cross are announced for acts of gallantry and exemplary conduct—for example, crew members who kept their plane in the air while the field was bombed, worked without rest to load for a mission, and scored direct hits on enemy transports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple award citations in the copy describe specific heroic actions (keeping aircraft airborne under attack, loading under fire, low-altitude attacks scoring hits) as the basis for decorations; these functionally describe the merit standards used in reporting award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for immediate call-up of men in protected industries / reserve occupations
rubrics_metrics.description: Men up to 40 years old who are in protected industries or reserve occupations are now liable for immediate call into the armed services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is reported as a policy affecting manpower and mobilization—context notes that previously classes could not supply the manpower needed and that older men in protected categories may be subject to call-up as part of reorganization and mobilization efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate procedural practice: referral of amendments to committee with instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senate may send proposed amendments to the relevant committee with instruction to hold hearings and report 'as soon as practicable,' a referral that typically delays immediate floor consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article example: Lee's alcohol amendment was sent to the Military Affairs Committee with instructions to hold hearings, effectively postponing consideration until after upcoming elections; reporters used this to explain legislative momentum and likely outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional oversight/investigation as means to verify administrative claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials (e.g., Secretary Ickes) stated no objection to a Congressional investigation of the Interior Department's administration of Puerto Rico affairs; such an investigation is presented as an appropriate measure to verify disputed statements and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: local leaders made allegations about conditions in Puerto Rico; Ickes welcomed an inquiry and offered to have specific statements enumerated so they could be verified beyond doubt—demonstrating the use of hearings/investigations as an accountability standard.
